children: fell sharply as its second-quarter earnings beat did not match some high-flying expectations. For FQ1, the retailer reported inside same-store sales growth of 3.2%, grocery and general merchandise same-store sales growth of 2.7%, and prepared food and dispensed beverage same-store sales growth of 4.8%. Operating expenses increased 8% during the quarter as store growth costs, higher credit-card fees, and higher labor expenses factored in.
Jefferies analyst Corey Tarlowe thinks Casey's

CASY delivered a strong quarter, with revenue of $5.68B, EBITDA of $485.1M, and EPS of $7.37, all exceeding expectations. "Despite CASY's broad-based strength across inside and fuel, elevated expectations and a premium valuation likely drove the AH pullback," noted Tarlowe. He said due to the continued comparable sales growth, margin expansion, and an unchanged outlook, the firm would recommend being buyers on the weakness.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Irene Nattel thinks the first-quarter results put Casey's

on strong footing to achieve F27 guidance as strong execution and fuel margins drove Q1 EPS to an above-consensus mark of $7.37. "CASY continues to earn its valuation premium, underpinned by attractive inside-store mix, unit growth, geographic concentration, and strong opex controls," highlighted Nattel.
In its post-earnings assessment, Bank of America maintained its Buy rating on Casey's
CASY’s given the strength of its inside sales, cost control management, and fuel margin enhancement ability.
slid 10.9% in premarket trading on Wednesday. The convenience store stock was up more than 40% on a year-to-date basis heading into the earnings release.

title: Casey's is defended by analysts after post-earnings slide
